mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 5-day forward returns is negative (or < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% indicates labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) from prior month signals weakening consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue expectations and generating negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when HOUST and RSAFS both decline from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) combined with rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates manufacturing contraction and labor market stress, reducing corporate profitability and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines and UNRATE rises from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO declines and UNRATE rises from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A higher real GDP level (GDPC1) reflects robust economic activity that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between GDPC1 and 20-day forward returns is negative (or < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.0% indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in < 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) from prior month signals labor market deterioration that reduces household income and consumption, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) from prior month indicates active monetary easing, which lowers equity discount rates and generates positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines from prior month.
